newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money dealers say NBC allocation on low side.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money dealers say NBC allocation on low side.

text.p: Dutch money market dealers said the total number of bids accepted for today's sale of Netherlands Bank Certificates (NBCs) was on the low side and some banks had stayed sidelined.
NBCs are used to drain structural money market surpluses and complement the cash reserve instrument.
The auctions are open to credit institutions registered in the Netherlands and deals are settled between the central bank and commercial banks.
Earlier today, the Dutch central bank accepted bids for NBCs totalling 765 million guilders at a yield of 2.88 percent.
"Business is slow all over," said one dealer, adding that many market players might be awaiting higher rates. The market has been under upward pressure for over a week now.
Call money rates were fractionally higher at 2.81/88 percent bid from 2.81 percent on Friday.
"Call is trading well above the special advances rate of 2.50 percent," said one dealer, adding it was about time for the call rate to edge closer to the advances rate.
The same dealer said banks might build up extra savings under the current three-month credit quota, which came into effect a week ago.
"They might build up extra savings, just to be on the safe side," said another dealer, adding the demand for call money had risen on this assumption.
Other money market rates remained high. Three-month deposits were trading at 2.86 percent.
The guilder traded at 112.16 per 100 marks from 112.15 on Friday.
